EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Middle East escalated significantly with the killing of two Israeli reservists and severe wounding of four others in southern Lebanon, prompting immediate Israeli retaliatory strikes and an evacuation order for Al-Mansouri. Simultaneously, crucial negotiations for reopening the Strait of Hormuz are reportedly nearing a temporary agreement between Iran and Oman, despite continued Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers and an Iranian warning of regional retaliation against US attacks.

IRAN
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian described his interaction with Supreme Leader Khamenei as "very complicated" but affirmed the Leader's support for his government and consensus on negotiations following a 12-out-of-13 vote in the Supreme National Security Council. Pezeshkian emphasized Iran's strength and resilience against adversaries, while reiterating Tehran's full support for any decisions made by Hamas's political leadership regarding negotiations. Brigadier General Mohammad Akrami-Nia stated the Iranian Army is fully prepared, modernizing systems, and expanding domestic capabilities. The IRGC Ground Force's Quds Headquarters arrested eight armed militants in Sistan and Baluchestan province, accused of various security-related offenses. UN Human Rights Commissioner reported at least 56 executions in Iran since March 19, including 27 protesters, for "security-related offenses." Hardliner Hossein Shariatmadari criticized the potential Strait of Hormuz deal, viewing it as relinquishing a key leverage point, while former Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif warned that uncontrolled tension with the US would hinder cooperation with partners like China and Russia.

ISRAEL
Two Israeli reservist soldiers, Maj. (res.) Harel Birenstock (34) and Sgt. Maj. (res.) Tamir Vaknin (33), were killed, and four others seriously wounded, by an explosive device in Majdal Zoun, southern Lebanon on 05 August during operations to clear Hezbollah infrastructure. Defense Minister Israel Katz instructed the army not to reduce reservist civil defense squads in Gaza border communities to maintain residents' security. An urgent discussion on the threat of drones within Israel was held by Minister Katz, aiming for a comprehensive operational and regulatory response. The long-range Arrow missile defense system underwent a successful pre-planned test. Prime Minister Netanyahu prematurely left a ceremony, citing "current military and political events," and stated that Israel's existence is non-negotiable, vowing to do "whatever is necessary" to ensure its future. He also rejected any US proposal that would disarm Hamas and manage Gaza, and affirmed Israel would not allow a Palestinian state.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF demolished an underground tunnel in the southern Gaza Strip containing dozens of rockets. Chief of Staff Zamir conducted a tour of Gaza, stating that Hamas has been significantly weakened and that operations will continue to remove threats and hold accountable those involved in the 07 October attacks. In the West Bank, 11 Palestinians were injured during Israeli forces' raids in the Qalandiya refugee camp, where a young Palestinian man was also violently detained. Israeli civilians reportedly set fire to several Palestinian homes in the village of Tuba, south of al-Khalil, injuring multiple Palestinians, including a child and a woman; the IDF condemned the incident and called for legal action. A reported "terrorist infiltration" in Tel Zion and Kokhav Ya'akov in Samaria was later confirmed as a false alarm caused by two suspicious Israeli vehicles. Hamas accused Israel of obstructing the Gaza ceasefire implementation and urged the US to pressure Israel to fulfill its obligations.

LEBANON
The killing of two Israeli reservists and severe injury of four others in Majdal Zoun, southern Lebanon, by an explosive device on 05 August sparked immediate Israeli military responses. The IDF launched "precise strikes" in southern Lebanon, specifically targeting Burj al-Shamali and Al-Mansouri, and issued an "urgent" evacuation warning for residents of Al-Mansouri to move at least 1 kilometer north. Lebanese media reported one dead and 11 wounded in an Israeli strike on a prayer room in Tebnine. The IDF accused Hezbollah of a "blatant violation of the ceasefire" as justification for its intensified operations. Approximately 15 Israeli civilians, identified as members of the Uri Tzafon Movement, illegally crossed the border into Lebanon near Ghajar after damaging the border fence; they were subsequently located and returned to Israel by IDF and Border Police forces, with the IDF condemning their actions as criminal and a danger to operational security.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Iraqi Ministry of Justice successfully won a lawsuit in Jordanian courts, recovering financial amounts for an Iraqi pharmaceutical company. The State Administration Coalition in Iraq condemned attacks on Iraqi armed forces, stressing the prohibition of using Iraqi territory for attacks against neighboring countries, and called for strict adherence to weapon restriction timelines after 30 September 2026. Saudi Arabia and Kuwait lodged a new protest with the United Nations against Iraq's maritime boundary maps, fearing severe repercussions for their relationship with Iraq and asserting Iraq's intent to seize oil and gas fields. An Iraqi politician, Aras Habib, issued a threat to invade Saudi Arabia. Unidentified warplanes were reported flying over Muthanna province in southern Iraq. The Hashed al-Shaabi denied reports of armed clashes in Samarra.

GULF STATES
A tanker transiting the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz reported two explosions in its vicinity, approximately 9 nautical miles southeast of Kumzar, Oman; the crew was unharmed. Yemeni Houthi forces claimed to have attacked the Saudi oil tanker "Daisy" in the Gulf of Aden with a ballistic missile, forcing it to return, as part of their "maritime blockade" against Saudi Arabia. This marks the eighth vessel targeted in their campaign. The UKMTO also reported a separate incident where an uncrewed surface vessel (USV) struck a ship in the Red Sea, 9 nautical miles from Mocha, Yemen, causing a fire and leading to the ship's sinking, though the crew was rescued. Iran reportedly warned Gulf states that any new US attack on Iran would result in Iranian retaliation against critical energy infrastructure across the region. Pakistan's Foreign Ministry spokesperson confirmed ongoing diplomatic engagement with other countries regarding the Middle East crisis and the Strait of Hormuz.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Israeli Casualties in Lebanon:** Two Israeli reservists, Maj. Harel Birenstock and Sgt. Maj. Tamir Vaknin, were killed, and four others seriously wounded, by an explosive device in Majdal Zoun, southern Lebanon, on 05 August.
2.  **Israeli Retaliatory Strikes & Evacuation:** Israel launched "precise strikes" in southern Lebanon, notably in Burj al-Shamali and Al-Mansouri, and issued an urgent evacuation order for Al-Mansouri, citing a "blatant violation of the ceasefire" by Hezbollah.
3.  **Hormuz Negotiations Progress:** Iran and Oman are reportedly nearing finalization of a joint statement on a new commercial shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, with coordinates agreed upon for a potential temporary 60-day agreement.
4.  **Houthi Tanker Attack:** Yemeni Houthi forces claimed a ballistic missile attack on the Saudi oil tanker "Daisy" in the Gulf of Aden, forcing it back, as part of their "maritime blockade" against Saudi Arabia.
5.  **US Missile Shortages:** Reports indicate US President Trump confronted Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over severe shortages of key US missile interceptors, impacting military options against Iran, with CNN reporting nearly 80% of key interceptors used.
6.  **Iranian Warning to Gulf States:** The IRGC warned Gulf states that any new US attack on Iran would trigger retaliation against critical energy infrastructure across the region.
7.  **Israeli Civilian Border Crossing:** Approximately 15 Israeli civilians from the Uri Tzafon Movement illegally crossed into Lebanon near Ghajar, damaging the border fence, prompting IDF condemnation and calls for legal action.
8.  **Iran Internal Executions:** The UN Human Rights Commissioner reported at least 56 executions in Iran since 19 March, including 27 protesters, for "security-related offenses."

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks in southern Lebanon are extremely high following the Israeli casualties and retaliatory strikes, coupled with the explicit IDF accusation of a Hezbollah ceasefire violation and the first evacuation order for a Lebanese village in weeks. The ongoing, complex negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz, despite apparent progress towards a temporary agreement, remain a critical flashpoint. Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers in the Gulf of Aden and Red Sea add to regional maritime insecurity. The US internal debate over munitions shortages could either constrain or embolden military actions, while Iran's warning of regional retaliation against any US attack raises the stakes for critical energy infrastructure. The Israeli government's strong stance against a Palestinian state and rejection of the US Gaza proposal further exacerbates the situation in Gaza and the West Bank, potentially leading to increased unrest and violence.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US, through various officials, is actively engaged in diplomatic efforts regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with President Trump signaling an imminent deal while also warning of severe military retaliation if talks fail. The US Treasury Department removed sanctions on Iraq's Fly Baghdad Airlines, signaling a limited de-escalation specific to Iraq. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt's Foreign Ministers continue to meet, with Pakistan emphasizing commitment to peace and security through dialogue in West Asia. Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated Israel has no intention for peace in Gaza. Germany opened a counter-terrorism investigation after an explosive drone was found near Ukrainian aircraft at Leipzig airport, with Russian actors suspected. Ukraine reported drone attacks on Russian territory and Russian attacks on Balakliya, while Russia claimed shooting down numerous Ukrainian drones and targeting military cargo ships. The Pentagon is drafting a new nuclear strategy for potential tactical use against China or Russia in regional conflicts. The EU Commission President announced 1.4 billion EUR from frozen Russian assets would be used for Ukraine. North Korea is reportedly deploying a missile unit to Russia's Voronezh region, signaling continued military support.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are notable contradictions regarding US-Iran interactions. President Trump claimed Iran called him to negotiate after the US prepared for a "biggest attack since WWII," a claim explicitly denied by Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi, who stated there were "no talks with the US in recent days." Furthermore, initial reports of the US Treasury Department removing "25 sanctions related to Iran" (yediotnews25) were clarified by Fox News and Kian Meli to be limited to the lifting of sanctions on the Iraqi Fly Baghdad Airlines and its fleet, with no broader change in US policy towards Iran. There is also a discrepancy in reporting the attack on a ship in the Red Sea: yediotnews25 and NAYA report a "huge explosion near a vessel," while VahidOnline states a USV "collided with this ship in the Red Sea," resulting in a fire and sinking. The claim by Israeli Wynet of a specific Israeli plan for "regime change" in Iran involving Kurdish forces and Ahmadinejad's management of street protests, dismissed by senior US officials as "unserious and baseless," appears to be an unverified and likely propagandistic assertion. The specific coordinates and conditions of the proposed Iran-Oman Hormuz deal, and its potential implications for transit fees and security, remain subject to varying interpretations and ongoing negotiation.
